title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
statement: Return the minimal length of a contiguous subarray of `nums` whose sum is at least `target`. If no such subarray exists, return 0. Every element is positive.
hints: Positive numbers mean the window sum grows as the right edge moves and shrinks as the left edge moves.
Expand until the sum is large enough, then shrink while it stays large enough.
Track the smallest window length seen during shrinking. Return 0 when the total sum is too small.

approaches.name: All subarrays
approaches.explanation: Extend each start until the sum reaches the target.

approaches.name: Positive sliding window
approaches.explanation: Each index is added and removed at most once.

editorial: This is the canonical variable-size window for a monotone condition. Add nums[right] into the sum. While the sum is at least target, update the best length and subtract nums[left]. Positivity is the invariant that lets you discard the left element forever.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def min_subarray_len(target: int, nums: list[int]) -> int:
    left = total = 0
    best = len(nums) + 1
    for right, value in enumerate(nums):
        total += value
        while total >= target:
            best = min(best, right - left + 1)
            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1
    return 0 if best > len(nums) else best
